look_here_first: LOOK AT THE LEAF BASE AND COLLAR: many stem blades are broadly lance-shaped, often with a heart-shaped (cordate) base; the true ligule is minute or apparently absent. Use the relatively few-flowered open panicle and a measured 2.1–3.2 mm spikelet as a second check. Leaf-base shape varies; never certify from one leaf alone.

best_field_traits: Perennial; unlike many rosette-grasses it may lack an obvious winter basal rosette.
Largest stem blades commonly 6–12 cm long and roughly 7–15 mm wide; often cordate at the base, but not consistently.
Sheath backs often hairless or sparsely hairy; marginal and collar hairs may still be conspicuous.
True ligule a minute fringe or absent; inspect at magnification.
Open, rather few-spikeleted spring panicles; spikelets broadly about 2.1–3.2 mm long.
crew_field_check: Start from the same rooted clump; note spring vs late-season growth.
Expose the collar and photograph the true ligule with a ruler; separate the blade-base cilia from collar hairs.
Measure at least three mature spikelets and examine glumes under magnification.
If collar or spikelet anatomy is absent, label as provisional Dichanthelium sp.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole clump showing presence/absence of basal rosette
stem leaf base laid flat against ruler
three mature spikelets with mm ruler.

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with D. oligosanthes, first check the presence of a broad winter rosette and measure the spikelets and ligules; measurements overlap at the margins. D. lindheimeri normally has much smaller, blunt spikelets and a conspicuous hair ligule; D. pedicellatum has narrow thin leaves and a short but distinct hair curtain at the collar. D. commutatum is not safely identified from an open panicle alone.
